terms.meaning: The valley that splits the Peninsular Plateau into the Malwa Plateau (north) and the Deccan Plateau (south).
A salt lake in the Thar desert.
Karnataka's hilly, rainy, forested belt between the coast and the Maidan, called the Sahyadri Ranges.
Karnataka's undulating plateau east of the Malnad, split by the Tungabhadra into north and south.

items.name: India's location and extent
items.formula: 8°N to 37°N and 68°E to 97°E, all in the Northern Hemisphere.
items.example: The Tropic of Cancer passes through the middle; seventh largest by area.

items.name: India's neighbours
items.formula: North-west: Pakistan, Afghanistan. North: China, Nepal, Bhutan. East: Bangladesh, Myanmar.
items.example: Sri Lanka lies across the Palk Strait and the Gulf of Mannar.

items.name: India's four physical divisions
items.formula: Northern Mountains, Northern Plains, Peninsular Plateaus and Coastal Plains.
items.example: Plus the islands and the Thar desert.

items.name: The Himalayas
items.formula: Mt. Everest (8848 m) is the world's highest; Mt. K2 or Godwin Austin (8611 m) is India's highest.
items.example: They block cold Central Asian winds and stop the monsoon to give rain.

items.name: The Northern Plains
items.formula: Built of alluvium from the Sutlej, Ganges and Brahmaputra.
items.example: Fertile and flat, so densely populated.

items.name: Peninsular Plateau peaks
items.formula: Aravallis' highest: Gurushikhar (1722 m). South India's highest: Anaimudi (2695 m) on the Anamalai hills.
items.example: Western and Eastern Ghats meet at the Nilgiris (Ooty).

items.name: India's coastal plains
items.formula: Western: narrow and rocky, from the Gulf of Kuch to Kanyakumari. Eastern: broader, from the Ganga delta to Kanyakumari.

items.name: India's islands
items.formula: 247 in all: 204 Andaman and Nicobar (volcanic rock) and 43 Lakshadweep (coral sand).
items.example: Andaman and Nicobar are in the Bay of Bengal; Lakshadweep in the Arabian Sea.

items.name: Thar desert
items.formula: In north-west India, about two-thirds of it in Rajasthan.
items.example: Sambhar is India's largest salt lake.

items.name: Karnataka's location
items.formula: 11°N to 18°N and 74°E to 78°E; eighth largest state; 31 districts and 227 taluks.
items.example: Neighbours: Maharashtra, Goa, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Kerala.

items.name: Karnataka's coastal plain
items.formula: About 324 km, from Goa to Kerala: Uttara Kannada, Udupi and Dakshina Kannada.
items.example: New Mangalore port is the "Gateway of Karnataka".

items.name: Malnad facts
items.formula: Agumbe gets the most rain in Karnataka; Mullayanagiri (1913 m) is the highest peak.

items.name: Northern and Southern Maidan
items.formula: North: flat basalt with black soil and low rain. South (Mysore Plateau): hilly, red soil, more rain.
items.example: Both slope east, with the Krishna-Bhima and the Kaveri.

items.name: Famous things from Karnataka
items.formula: Mudhol Hounds; Ilkal silk sarees; Athani slippers; Davangere was the "Manchester of Karnataka".

mistakes.text: Everest is the world's highest peak, but India's highest peak is K2 (Godwin Austin).
Andaman and Nicobar are volcanic rock; Lakshadweep is coral.
Northern Maidan has black soil; Southern Maidan has red soil.
